svg.title: DriveSTA teaser: temporal driving examples, metrics and scored alternatives
svg.desc: Figure 1 revision: remove only the outer method border and compact internal vertical gaps while preserving all text, nodes, photos and connections. The four inner method borders remain. The metric chart preserves all marks and scores under uniform scaling. The two-column demo arrangement is retained: two HUGSIM cases with six frames each and two NAVSIM 1x5 comparisons, modestly enlarged at equal height and original aspect ratio. No wording or source geometry changes.

svg.title: Training targets and online computation in four driving planners
svg.text: Screened targets from the same scene

svg.title: DriveSTA: five methods per metric
svg.desc: Each bar shows (score minus reference)/(DriveSTA score minus reference). Display references by sector: Navtest PDMS 94, Navtest EPDMS 89, Navhard EPDMS 47, HD-Score 35, Route completion 47. DriveSTA has normalized length 1 on all five metrics; WA-JEPA has greater length for its higher Navtest EPDMS 91.7. Only DriveSTA is annotated with a face: a plain smile for each displayed DriveSTA bar. Face fill and eyes match the lower-right Figure 1. Printed values are original scores, not normalized scores. Baselines are display references, not zero points of the original metrics. The selected comparisons are not a complete ranking. Methods use their best reported family configuration except FPD-Drive Navhard, where the user supplied the comparable-data result 55.8. FPD-Drive PDMS uses the manuscript value 95.5. Colors identify methods consistently across all metrics. This is a standalone teaser component; no manuscript source or original Figure 1 has been changed.

svg.title: HUGSIM hard scene: matched-observation plans at 2.00 s
svg.desc: Original recorded camera image. DriveSTA and FPD-Drive Base predictions use the same observations; calibrated ground projection and vehicle occlusion. Scene scores are evaluated from separate closed-loop runs.

g.desc: DriveSTA and FPD-Drive Base trajectories from the same observations. Only genuinely visible camera projections are drawn; original images and times are retained.
